title: 1892, Changes after WA enters Union
object_transcript:

The entrance of the State of Wash into the Union brot chgs to the schl on LT. In 1892 a representative of the staff of the State Supt of Public Instr condemned the log schlhse so it was abandoned. The logs from this 1st schl bldg were used in the construction of Loganita Lodge... The site of the second schlhse was on the southern end of the island. (see other notes---same site as 1st)... This acre-tract was donated for a consid of 1.00 to Schl Dist No 32 by Theodore Peterson. The deed filed April 9, 1892 specified no restrictions. Here was erected a frame bldg made of machine-sawed boards. This second schlhse was also a one-room structure. To finance this new bldg the schl dist sold bonds amtg to $1000. on which rate of interest was 8%. title: 1897, Establishment of private school
object_transcript:
(113) Pgs 27-28
As the island continued to attract settlers, the schl population increased. As the settlers spread over the isl it became difficult for some of the younger pupils, esp to get to and frm schl. Often during the winter, they would have to start to schl by the light of a lantern and ret home the same way. Acc to Charles Granger "For this reason a private school was held on the island with Elizabeth Burroughs as the teacher. this school was held in a chicken coop behind what is now the Willows resort. It had an enrollment of 5 or 6 young pupils, but was discontinued after only one year." (See Dec 1897... Miss Isabell McDermoth is teaching private school on LI)
(Records indicate it was not discontinued... see notes from 1897 on to time Dist 32 acknowledges 2 schools) A real problem existed for a schoolhouse located at either extreme of the island would be at a prohibitive distance for any small child to walk, if he chanced to live at the opposite end of the island.
